ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A sample of some $N_2O_5$ gas is placed in a sealed container and allowed to decompose. The concentration of the $N_2O_5$ is tracked over time, and the results are plotted on the graph. What are the possible units of the rate constant for this reaction?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The graph has the vertical axis labeled [N2O5] and the horizontal axis labeled Time (s). The plotted concentration starts near 1.0 and decreases rapidly at first, then more slowly, forming an exponentially decreasing curve. Reasoning: An exponential decay in reactant concentration versus time is characteristic of a first-order decomposition. For a first-order reaction, the integrated rate law is [N2O5] = [N2O5]0 e^(-kt). The exponent kt must be unitless. Since time t is measured in seconds, k must have units of inverse seconds.
